diagrams.title: x402 alternative path: escrow flow with the auth-capture scheme
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: x402 alternative path: escrow flow with the auth-capture scheme. 4 participants: Client (agent), Resource server, Facilitator, and AuthCaptureEscrow (EVM). 9 steps, 4 crossing a trust boundary, 2 failure branches. Based on x402 v2.0 (2025-12-09). Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: POST /jobs (no payment). Step 2: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with an auth-capture entry. Step 3: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (one authorization). Step 4: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle (authorize: place the hold). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 5: Facilitator to AuthCaptureEscrow (EVM): authorize on AuthCaptureEscrow. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 6: Resource server to Resource server: Run the job and meter it. Step 7: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle (payload.type capture). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The server never captures: After captureDeadline the client can call reclaim directly on the escrow contract. If The buyer is unhappy later: The server can relay refund until refundDeadline. Step 8: Facilitator to AuthCaptureEscrow (EVM): capture 0.75 USDC. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 9: Resource server to Client (agent): 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE.
lines: Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: POST /jobs (no payment).
Step 2: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with an auth-capture entry.
Step 3: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (one authorization).
Step 4: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle (authorize: place the hold). This step crosses a trust boundary.
Step 5: Facilitator to AuthCaptureEscrow (EVM): authorize on AuthCaptureEscrow. This step crosses a trust boundary.
Step 6: Resource server to Resource server: Run the job and meter it.

Step 7: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle (payload.type capture). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The server never captures: After captureDeadline the client can call reclaim directly on the escrow contract. If The buyer is unhappy later: The server can relay refund until refundDeadline.
Step 8: Facilitator to AuthCaptureEscrow (EVM): capture 0.75 USDC. This step crosses a trust boundary.
Step 9: Resource server to Client (agent): 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE.

diagrams.title: x402 failure: the authorization expired (validBefore in the past)
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: x402 failure: the authorization expired (validBefore in the past). 3 participants: Client (agent), Resource server, and Facilitator. 5 steps, 1 crossing a trust boundary. Based on x402 v2.0 (2025-12-09). Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. Step 2: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 3: Facilitator to Resource server: Return isValid false (valid_before). Step 4: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with a fresh PAYMENT-REQUIRED. Step 5: Client (agent) to Client (agent): Sign again with a new window and nonce.
lines: Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE.
Step 2: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify. This step crosses a trust boundary.
Step 3: Facilitator to Resource server: Return isValid false (valid_before).
Step 4: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with a fresh PAYMENT-REQUIRED.
Step 5: Client (agent) to Client (agent): Sign again with a new window and nonce.

diagrams.title: x402 failure: the facilitator is down or times out
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: x402 failure: the facilitator is down or times out. 4 participants: Client (agent), Resource server, Facilitator, and Base Sepolia. 5 steps, 3 crossing a trust boundary, 1 failure branch. Based on x402 v2.0 (2025-12-09). Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. Step 2: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify (no answer). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 3: Resource server to Client (agent): 502 Bad Gateway. Step 4: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle (times out). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The facilitator answers settlement_pending: Non-terminal. The response carries the broadcast hash; the server checks it on chain and retries at most once. Step 5: Resource server to Base Sepolia: Reconcile: look up the transaction. This step crosses a trust boundary.
lines: Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE.
Step 2: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify (no answer). This step crosses a trust boundary.
Step 3: Resource server to Client (agent): 502 Bad Gateway.

Step 4: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle (times out). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The facilitator answers settlement_pending: Non-terminal. The response carries the broadcast hash; the server checks it on chain and retries at most once.
Step 5: Resource server to Base Sepolia: Reconcile: look up the transaction. This step crosses a trust boundary.

diagrams.title: x402 failure: the payer balance is too low
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: x402 failure: the payer balance is too low. 4 participants: Client (agent), Resource server, Facilitator, and Base Sepolia. 6 steps, 2 crossing a trust boundary, 1 failure branch. Based on x402 v2.0 (2025-12-09). Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. Step 2: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 3: Facilitator to Resource server: Return isValid false (insufficient_funds). If The balance was enough at verify time but dropped before settle: Verify passes and the handler runs. Steps 4 to 6 show the settle-time variant. Step 4: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle (balance dropped after verify). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 5: Facilitator to Resource server: Return success false (insufficient_funds). Step 6: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with PAYMENT-RESPONSE success false.
lines: Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE.
Step 2: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify. This step crosses a trust boundary.

Step 3: Facilitator to Resource server: Return isValid false (insufficient_funds). If The balance was enough at verify time but dropped before settle: Verify passes and the handler runs. Steps 4 to 6 show the settle-time variant.
Step 4: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle (balance dropped after verify). This step crosses a trust boundary.
Step 5: Facilitator to Resource server: Return success false (insufficient_funds).
Step 6: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with PAYMENT-RESPONSE success false.

diagrams.title: x402 failure: a used authorization is sent again (replayed nonce)
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: x402 failure: a used authorization is sent again (replayed nonce). 4 participants: Client (agent), Resource server, Facilitator, and Base Sepolia. 6 steps, 2 crossing a trust boundary. Based on x402 v2.0 (2025-12-09). Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. Step 2: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 3: Facilitator to Base Sepolia: Read authorizationState(from, nonce). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 4: Base Sepolia to Facilitator: Return true (nonce used). Step 5: Facilitator to Resource server: Return isValid false (nonce already used). Step 6: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with a fresh PAYMENT-REQUIRED.
lines: Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE.
Step 2: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify. This step crosses a trust boundary.
Step 3: Facilitator to Base Sepolia: Read authorizationState(from, nonce). This step crosses a trust boundary.
Step 4: Base Sepolia to Facilitator: Return true (nonce used).
Step 5: Facilitator to Resource server: Return isValid false (nonce already used).
Step 6: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with a fresh PAYMENT-REQUIRED.

diagrams.title: x402 failure: the signed recipient does not match payTo
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: x402 failure: the signed recipient does not match payTo. 3 participants: Client (agent), Resource server, and Facilitator. 5 steps, 1 crossing a trust boundary. Step 5: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with a fresh PAYMENT-REQUIRED.

diagrams.title: x402 payment lifecycle (V2, all three payment flows)
diagrams.description: State diagram: x402 payment lifecycle (V2, all three payment flows). 11 states: Unpaid request, Payment required (402), Payload received, Verified, Committed before execution, Handler executed, Settlement pending, Settled, Rejected, Responded 200, and Voided or reclaimed. Starts in Unpaid request. Ends in Rejected, Responded 200, and Voided or reclaimed. 16 transitions. From Unpaid request to Payment required (402) when Server sends 402 (HTTP 402 + PAYMENT-REQUIRED). From Payment required (402) to Payload received when Client retries with a signed payload (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header). From Payload received to Rejected when Malformed payload or unsupported scheme, network or flow (HTTP 400). From Payload received to Verified when authorization flow: facilitator returns isValid true (POST /verify). From Payload received to Rejected when isValid false or facilitator unreachable (POST /verify). From Payload received to Committed before execution when upfront or escrow flow: first settle succeeds (POST /settle). From Verified to Handler executed when Handler runs. From Committed before execution to Handler executed when Handler runs. From Handler executed to Settled when authorization flow: settle succeeds, or escrow: capture succeeds (POST /settle). From Handler executed to Settlement pending when Settle broadcast but not confirmed, or timed out (POST /settle). From Settlement pending to Settled when Server reconciles on chain and finds the transfer. From Settlement pending to Rejected when Reconciliation shows no transfer and one retry fails (POST /settle). From Handler executed to Rejected when Settle fails (for example insufficient_funds) (HTTP 402 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE success false). From Handler executed to Voided or reclaimed when escrow: server voids the hold, or the client reclaims after captureDeadline (POST /settle with payload.type void). From Settled to Responded 200 when Server returns the resource (HTTP 200 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE). From Handler executed to Responded 200 when upfront: payment already settled, server returns the resource (HTTP 200 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE).
lines: From Unpaid request to Payment required (402) when Server sends 402 (HTTP 402 + PAYMENT-REQUIRED).
From Payment required (402) to Payload received when Client retries with a signed payload (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header).
From Payload received to Rejected when Malformed payload or unsupported scheme, network or flow (HTTP 400).
From Payload received to Verified when authorization flow: facilitator returns isValid true (POST /verify).
From Payload received to Rejected when isValid false or facilitator unreachable (POST /verify).
From Payload received to Committed before execution when upfront or escrow flow: first settle succeeds (POST /settle).
From Verified to Handler executed when Handler runs.
From Committed before execution to Handler executed when Handler runs.
From Handler executed to Settled when authorization flow: settle succeeds, or escrow: capture succeeds (POST /settle).
From Handler executed to Settlement pending when Settle broadcast but not confirmed, or timed out (POST /settle).
From Settlement pending to Settled when Server reconciles on chain and finds the transfer.
From Settlement pending to Rejected when Reconciliation shows no transfer and one retry fails (POST /settle).
From Handler executed to Rejected when Settle fails (for example insufficient_funds) (HTTP 402 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE success false).
From Handler executed to Voided or reclaimed when escrow: server voids the hold, or the client reclaims after captureDeadline (POST /settle with payload.type void).
From Settled to Responded 200 when Server returns the resource (HTTP 200 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE).
From Handler executed to Responded 200 when upfront: payment already settled, server returns the resource (HTTP 200 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE).

diagrams.title: x402 alternative path: upfront flow with the exact scheme on Lightning
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: x402 alternative path: upfront flow with the exact scheme on Lightning. 4 participants: Client (agent), Resource server, Facilitator, and Lightning Network. 8 steps, 2 crossing a trust boundary, 3 failure branches. Based on x402 v2.0 (2025-12-09). Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: GET /article/A. Step 2: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with a fresh BOLT11 invoice. Step 3: Client (agent) to Lightning Network: Pay the invoice. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The invoice expired (maxTimeoutSeconds equals the invoice expiry): The payment fails; the client requests a new 402. Step 4: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (preimage). Step 5: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle (no /verify). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The preimage does not match, or the payment hash was already recorded: Settle fails and the handler does not run. A replay is refused. Step 6: Facilitator to Resource server: Return SettleResponse success true. Step 7: Resource server to Resource server: Run the handler. If The handler fails after settlement: The client paid for nothing; any remedy is the server's own arrangement. Step 8: Resource server to Client (agent): 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE.
lines: Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: GET /article/A.
Step 2: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with a fresh BOLT11 invoice.

Step 3: Client (agent) to Lightning Network: Pay the invoice. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The invoice expired (maxTimeoutSeconds equals the invoice expiry): The payment fails; the client requests a new 402.
Step 4: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (preimage).

Step 5: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle (no /verify). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The preimage does not match, or the payment hash was already recorded: Settle fails and the handler does not run. A replay is refused.
Step 6: Facilitator to Resource server: Return SettleResponse success true.
Step 7: Resource server to Resource server: Run the handler. If The handler fails after settlement: The client paid for nothing; any remedy is the server's own arrangement.
Step 8: Resource server to Client (agent): 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE.

diagrams.title: x402 V2 over HTTP: exact scheme, authorization payment flow
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: x402 V2 over HTTP: exact scheme, authorization payment flow. 4 participants: Client (agent), Resource server, Facilitator, and Base Sepolia. 13 steps, 4 crossing a trust boundary, 10 failure branches. Based on x402 v2.0 (2025-12-09). Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: GET /weather (no payment header). Step 2: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 Payment Required with PAYMENT-REQUIRED. If A route has no registered scheme: Since @x402/core 2.25.0 the SDK throws an error instead of answering 402 with an empty accepts list. Step 3: Client (agent) to Client (agent): Choose an accepts entry, check limits, sign EIP-712. If Amount is above the spend cap or the asset is not allowed: The SDK rejects the entry; if no entry is left, no payment is created. If The entry names a paymentFlow the client does not recognize: The client must skip that entry. Step 4: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry GET /weather with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. If The header is malformed: The server answers 400 (invalid payment). Step 5: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The facilitator is unreachable or times out: See the facilitator-down flow: the Express middleware answers 502 and the handler does not run. Step 6: Facilitator to Base Sepolia: Read balance and nonce state, simulate. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 7: Facilitator to Resource server: Return VerifyResponse isValid true. If isValid is false (for example expired window, wrong recipient, used nonce, low balance): The server answers 402 and the handler does not run. See the failure flows. Step 8: Resource server to Resource server: Run the handler. If The handler fails: The server does not settle, so the client is not charged (an SDK hook, settleOnCancel, can change this). Step 9: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The settle call times out: The outcome is indeterminate: the transfer may still confirm, so the server must reconcile before it retries. Step 10: Facilitator to Base Sepolia: Broadcast transferWithAuthorization. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The nonce was consumed in the meantime or the balance dropped: The transaction reverts; the facilitator returns success false. Step 11: Base Sepolia to Facilitator: Return transaction receipt. Step 12: Facilitator to Resource server: Return SettleResponse success true. If errorReason is settlement_pending: Non-terminal: the transaction was broadcast but not confirmed. The response carries the hash, and the server reconciles before it decides. Step 13: Resource server to Client (agent): 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE.
lines: Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: GET /weather (no payment header).

Step 2: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 Payment Required with PAYMENT-REQUIRED. If A route has no registered scheme: Since @x402/core 2.25.0 the SDK throws an error instead of answering 402 with an empty accepts list.

Step 3: Client (agent) to Client (agent): Choose an accepts entry, check limits, sign EIP-712. If Amount is above the spend cap or the asset is not allowed: The SDK rejects the entry; if no entry is left, no payment is created. If The entry names a paymentFlow the client does not recognize: The client must skip that entry.
Step 4: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry GET /weather with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. If The header is malformed: The server answers 400 (invalid payment).

Step 5: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The facilitator is unreachable or times out: See the facilitator-down flow: the Express middleware answers 502 and the handler does not run.
Step 6: Facilitator to Base Sepolia: Read balance and nonce state, simulate. This step crosses a trust boundary.

Step 7: Facilitator to Resource server: Return VerifyResponse isValid true. If isValid is false (for example expired window, wrong recipient, used nonce, low balance): The server answers 402 and the handler does not run. See the failure flows.
Step 8: Resource server to Resource server: Run the handler. If The handler fails: The server does not settle, so the client is not charged (an SDK hook, settleOnCancel, can change this).

Step 9: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The settle call times out: The outcome is indeterminate: the transfer may still confirm, so the server must reconcile before it retries.

Step 10: Facilitator to Base Sepolia: Broadcast transferWithAuthorization. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The nonce was consumed in the meantime or the balance dropped: The transaction reverts; the facilitator returns success false.
Step 11: Base Sepolia to Facilitator: Return transaction receipt.

Step 12: Facilitator to Resource server: Return SettleResponse success true. If errorReason is settlement_pending: Non-terminal: the transaction was broadcast but not confirmed. The response carries the hash, and the server reconciles before it decides.
Step 13: Resource server to Client (agent): 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE.
